title: A Chill and Cozy Look at Cryptic Explorers
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JH6X6472Gdk

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes Cryptic Explorers, freshly delivered from Tempest Tome's Kickstarter. He'd forgotten to finalise his pledge and thanks them for letting him pay shipping late. He'd interviewed the designers in a noisy Seattle bar years earlier, and the bold black-and-white art and death-realm lore have him excited. He's also apprehensive: it's a competitive one-versus-many game, and he admits he's bad at being "the one," especially against friends who play hardcore PC strategy games. He hopes it works two-handed, or that someone designs an automa.

The premise: a shadowy organisation, Nauticus, sends squads of cryptonauts through the Maw of Thanatos into the realms of death to gather three Knowledge of Death cards and teleport home with them. A single opposing player is a goddess of death who summons monsters. He leafs through dozens of cryptonaut cards, including Hugo Price, "the director," who looks like an office worker stuck in torture-armor, and spots core-game and elite markings. The box holds three goddesses, double-sided realm boards, a realm book and an optional story book with eight campaigns. The Alpha Return expansion adds three more goddesses and six prequel explorers.

The corner clipper gets a workout. The boards are his favourite part: even if the game never hits the table, he'll use them as dungeons for solo Mörk Borg.

----

Daniel plans to use these boards for solo RPGs whatever happens with the game. Have you repurposed a board game's maps or components for something else entirely?
